unit.title: Numbers and Operations Around Us
unit.about_unit: Explores how human travel, trade, measurement, and recording large quantities led to five-digit numbers (ten thousands), multi-digit multiplication, division arrays, and multiplicative reasoning.

facilitation_guide.headline: Real-World Contexts
facilitation_guide.text: Connect numbers with train tickets, odometer readings, and village populations.

facilitation_guide.headline: Base-10 Manipulatives
facilitation_guide.text: Emphasize grouping 10 of any unit into 1 of the next higher unit using visual tokens.

chapter.title: We the Travellers — II
chapter.tagline: Mastering number groups, equal sums, distance calculations, and magic hexagons
chapter.overview: Continuing their travels, children analyze number groups to make their sums equal by swapping elements. They read road milestone maps to compute multi-leg journey distances, and solve magic hexagons using computational patterns.

sections.title: Equal Sum Groups: Interchanging Pairs
sections.subtitle: Balancing sum totals across two number sets

storyNarrative.dialogue: Group A sums to 54 and Group B sums to 46. If we swap one number from Group A with one from Group B, can we balance them both to 50?

concept.heading: Sum Balancing by Half-Difference
concept.keyRule: To balance two sets with difference D, exchange two numbers whose difference is exactly D / 2.

sections.title: The Travel Milestone Map: Distance Calculations
sections.subtitle: Adding and subtracting multi-leg travel segments

storyNarrative.dialogue: The highway milestone says Delhi is 185 km away and Jaipur is 260 km in the opposite direction. How far is Delhi from Jaipur?

concept.heading: Collinear Distance Addition
concept.keyRule: When travelling past a milestone between two cities, the total distance between the cities equals the sum of the two opposite distances.

sections.title: Magic Hexagons: Computational Patterns
sections.subtitle: Discovering multiplicative and additive relationships in geometric layouts

storyNarrative.dialogue: In this magic hexagon, the number in the square between two circles is the product of the numbers in those circles!

concept.heading: Relational Constraint Solving
concept.keyRule: If circle A and circle B connect to square S, then S = A × B. We can work backward: A = S ÷ B.
